matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal); you cannot rotate the stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before moving any stick, check its orientation and ensure the new position uses the same orientation.
matchstick.example: Moved a diagonal stick and placed it as a vertical, creating an invalid character.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Throughout the whole transformation, keep the total stick count unchanged.
matchstick.example: Removed a vertical stick from an I and did not place it elsewhere, effectively discarding a stick.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a valid operator (+, -, =); no partial symbols are allowed.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After the move, inspect each character to confirm it matches a permitted symbol.
matchstick.example: Resulted in a non‑standard numeral like 'XLX' after moving a stick.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and ensure the equality holds after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After constructing the new equation, compute its numeric value before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Produced the equation 'XX = XIX - XX', which does not satisfy the arithmetic equality.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V each consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, each must still contain two diagonal sticks, i.e., you cannot leave them with a single diagonal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When relocating a diagonal, ensure the source X or V retains both of its diagonals.
matchstick.example: Took a diagonal from a V, leaving it with only one diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching ‘Correct version of the equation: <equation>’, with uppercase letters and collapsed whitespace.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When writing the final answer, output only the required line in the exact format.
matchstick.example: Omitted the required final line or added extra spaces, causing the answer to be rejected.

matchstick.title: Intra‑character V↔X transformation
matchstick.principle: To change a V to an X (or X to a V) and adjust the value by 5, reposition one of the character’s own diagonal sticks within the same character; do not take a diagonal from another character, which would invalidate the source.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the arithmetic difference between sides is exactly 5 (or a multiple of 5) and the equation contains a V or X that can be altered without affecting other symbols.
matchstick.example: Moved a diagonal from one character to another, breaking the source V, instead of repositioning it within the same V.

matchstick.title: Preserve exactly one equals sign
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one ‘=’ operator; you cannot remove or add equals signs.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before finalizing the move, verify that the ‘=’ sign still consists of two horizontal sticks.
matchstick.example: Removed a horizontal stick from the '=' sign, turning it into a '-' sign.

matchstick.title: Target numeral based on arithmetic difference
matchstick.principle: Compute the Arabic values of both sides, find the difference, and identify a numeral that can be altered by moving a single stick to adjust its value by that amount (e.g., V↔X for a difference of 5, add/remove I for a difference of 1).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before moving a stick, use the numeric difference to decide which numeral to modify.
matchstick.example: Changed a numeral that did not affect the needed value adjustment, leaving the equation unbalanced.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer from I to V/X to create VI or XI
matchstick.principle: If the needed value change is 1, you can move a vertical stick from an I to a V (making VI) or to an X (making XI), ensuring the source I remains a valid numeral (e.g., by creating another I).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the arithmetic difference is 1 and the equation contains an I and a V or X that can accept a vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Moved a vertical stick from an I to a V, leaving the original I empty and invalid.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on making a syntactically valid transformation without computing the numeric values of the resulting equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After proposing a new equation, convert all Roman numerals to Arabic numbers and confirm the equality holds before finalizing.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model forgets the strict output requirement or adds extra text/whitespace.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure the response ends with a line exactly 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>', using uppercase letters and collapsed whitespace.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes moving a stick can be done by simply deleting it from the source character.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always place the moved stick onto another character or location, preserving the total stick count.

matchstick.description: Breaking a numeral by moving a stick away, leaving an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model does not consider the validity of the source character after removal of a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Verify that after removing a stick, the source character still forms a legal Roman numeral.

matchstick.description: Creating invalid Roman numeral (e.g., IIII, invalid ordering)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on stick placement without checking Roman numeral syntax rules.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After transformation, check that each numeral follows standard Roman numeral conventions (no more than three repeats, correct subtractive patterns, proper ordering).
